metadata.title: Teaching quality and student reading outcomes: Evidence from a longitudinal study from grade 5 to 7

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses NEPS longitudinal cohort data for Germany, restricting the analytic sample to students in main regular schools who remained at the same schools between grade 5 and grade 7, and excluding students with missing data on attended German class and on teacher information availability. To generalize to the underlying student population in Germany, the authors apply NEPS sampling weights that account for different sampling probabilities and initial and wave-specific nonresponse (w_t_cal). The models are estimated with school-fixed effects (absorbing school-level variation) and student controls measured in grade 5. Because the analysis is regression-based (not ML prediction), replicate weights are not reported; the key design feature is the use of sampling weights for population representativeness.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used NEPS starting cohort of grade 5 students in Germany, followed from school year 2010/2011 to grade 7 in 2012/2013. Included only students from the main regular school survey who remained at the same schools between grades 5 and 7; excluded students who changed schools between grades 5 and 7 or repeated a grade. Excluded students with missing data on the attended German class. Further excluded students who attended German classes for which no teacher information on teaching quality was available in grades 5, 6, and 7. Covered 15 of 16 federal states (Berlin excluded due to transition timing differences); students were nested in 150 schools.

main_findings.dataset_used: NEPS longitudinal cohort (Germany) Grade 5→7 Reading competence (WLE scores), grade 7 outcome
main_findings.performance_metrics: School-fixed effect regression (standardized coefficients). Main model: teaching quality components jointly show mostly non-significant effects; R2 values reported across model variants: 0.15 (no school-fixed effects), 0.27 (with school-fixed effects). Specific teaching-quality effects in the school-fixed effect model: none significant after accounting for prior covariates; robustness checks and Bonferroni correction indicate no reliable effects.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using NEPS longitudinal cohort (Germany) Grade 5→7 reading competence the study leveraged prior reading competence and baseline attitudes plus demographic and socioeconomic controls to model grade 7 reading competence, finding that none of the 10 teaching quality components had a measurable effect on student reading achievement once prior performance and school-fixed effects were included. This indicates that, in this tracked German German-language classroom context, questionnaire-based teaching quality dimensions may not translate into detectable short-run reading gains, suggesting policy should prioritize other levers (e.g., instructional effectiveness measured with stronger observational/learning-gain indicators) rather than relying on these specific teaching-quality survey scales.

main_findings.dataset_used: NEPS longitudinal cohort (Germany) Grade 5→7 Attitudes towards reading (mean scale), grade 7 outcome
main_findings.performance_metrics: School-fixed effect regression (standardized coefficients). Main model: only 'Evaluation' shows a very small significant association with attitudes towards reading in the school-fixed effect specification (β ≈ -0.05, SE ≈ 0.02), but after Bonferroni correction it is no longer significant; R2 values reported: 0.23 (with school-fixed effects). Cross-sectional associations largely vanish after controlling for prior attitudes.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using NEPS longitudinal cohort (Germany) Grade 5→7 attitudes towards reading the study leveraged prior attitudes and baseline student controls to model grade 7 reading attitudes, finding that teaching quality components had no meaningful longitudinal effects except for a very small 'evaluation' association that became non-significant after Bonferroni correction. This indicates that these teaching-quality survey dimensions are unlikely to be effective targets for improving students’ reading motivation in the short term, and that future policy-relevant measurement should focus on more robust instructional indicators and learning mechanisms.

data.outcome_summary: This longitudinal study uses NEPS data from Germany, following a grade 5 cohort to grade 7 (2010/2011 to 2012/2013) and analyzing students in main regular schools who stayed in the same schools between grades 5 and 7. Reading competence is measured with linked paper-pencil tests in grades 5 and 7 and analyzed using WLE scores (with reliabilities reported for grade 5 and grade 7). The authors estimate school-fixed effect regression models with a rich set of student controls measured in grade 5 and 10 teacher- and student-reported teaching quality scales aggregated across grades 5–7. Across specifications, teaching quality components show mostly non-significant effects on grade 7 reading competence and reading attitudes; the only small effect for attitudes (evaluation) disappears after Bonferroni correction. Missing data are handled via predictive mean matching with multiple imputations combined using Rubin’s rules, and sampling weights (w_t_cal) are used for population generalization. The study is not an ML prediction paper and therefore does not report ML metrics or model selection.
